issues.legal_issue: Interim payments made after an income-producing estate is taken, but before final compensation is determined, are capital receipts when they compensate for the loss of the income-producing asset rather than for the loss of interest on compensation.
material_facts: An estate vested in the government, depriving its former holders of the income-producing asset.
The former holders received recurring interim payments before the compensation for the estate was finally determined.

The amount of the interim payments was calculated by reference to the income the former holders would have received had they continued to own the estate, rather than by reference to estimated compensation.
The former holders were not entitled to the final compensation until it was determined, and the interim payments were not fixed as interest on that compensation.
issues.conclusion: The interim payments compensated the former holders for the loss of their income-producing asset and were capital receipts, not taxable revenue receipts.
issues.legal_principle: The character of a receipt depends on its substance, not the label given to it or the method used to calculate it. Section 3(e) treated the former holders as entitled only to compensation for the taking of their estates; sections 50(2) and 50(8) did not make the interim payments interest or exclude their character as compensation for recurring loss caused by taking an income-producing asset. Because final compensation became payable only after determination under section 39, and the interim payments were based on lost income rather than estimated compensation, they were not payments for being kept out of money already due. The Court relied on Dr. Sham Lal v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Punjab, for the distinction between interest and compensation; Senairam Doongarmall v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Assam, and Simpson v. Executors of Bonner Maurice, for the principle that the quality and substance of a payment determine its character. It distinguished Raja Rameshwara Rao v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Hyderabad, and Chandroji Rao v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Madhya Pradesh, and disapproved Kumara Rajah of Venkatagiri v. Income-tax Officer.

rule.if: income_tax_receipt_classification and income_producing_asset_taken and interim_payment_based_on_lost_income and final_compensation_not_yet_determined and not interim_payment_based_on_estimated_compensation

predicates.income_tax_receipt_classification: The proceeding requires a determination of whether a receipt is taxable income.
predicates.income_producing_asset_taken: The government took an asset that had produced income for its former holders.
predicates.interim_payment_based_on_lost_income: The government calculated recurring interim payments by reference to income the former holders lost when the asset was taken.
predicates.final_compensation_not_yet_determined: The former holders received the interim payments before their entitlement to final compensation had been determined.
predicates.interim_payment_based_on_estimated_compe: The government calculated the interim payments by reference to an estimate of the final compensation.
predicates.receipt_is_capital_not_taxable: The receipt is a capital receipt and is not taxable as revenue income.

issues.definition: When a proceeding classifies a receipt for income-tax purposes, and the government takes an income-producing asset and makes interim payments based on lost income before final compensation is determined, those payments are capital receipts rather than taxable revenue income if they are not based on estimated compensation.
